prompt: Robert-Houdin said he wore ordinary evening dress and avoided any eccentric costume.
explanation: His memoirs say he abstained from any eccentric costume and kept to the attire polite society accepted for evening dress.

prompt: Which of these was one of Robert-Houdin's own rules for his performances?
options: Make no puns or play upon words
Always wear a wizard's robe
Say that the tricks are real magic
Never use ordinary playing cards
correctAnswer: Make no puns or play upon words
explanation: He set himself a rule to make no puns or play upon words, and never to be guilty of a mystification.

prompt: In the Gentleman's Peek, what do you do before the spectator lifts off a packet?
options: Glimpse the bottom card of the deck, which becomes your key
Glimpse the top card of the deck
Ask them to sign a card
Shuffle the deck thoroughly
correctAnswer: Glimpse the bottom card of the deck, which becomes your key
explanation: The bottom card is the key; when your half is dropped on their packet it lies directly on the card they looked at.

prompt: In the Gentleman's Peek the spectator looks at the _____ card of the packet they lift off.
explanation: The top card of their packet is the one your key lands on when you drop your half on it.

prompt: Match each name or term to its description:

pairs.right: Opened a small theater at the Palais Royal in 1845
Added an i to Houdin's name and wrote The Unmasking in 1908
Reissued by Cambridge; first published in 1868
The 6♦ glimpsed at the bottom, dropped on their packet

explanation: Each fits what the lesson reports about the person, the book or the trick.

prompt: A friend says Houdini worshipped Robert-Houdin all his life. What is closest to the truth?
options: He took the name in admiration but in 1908 called his hero a pretender
He never read Robert-Houdin's books
He always praised him in print
Robert-Houdin was his teacher
correctAnswer: He took the name in admiration but in 1908 called his hero a pretender
explanation: The Unmasking of Robert-Houdin calls him a mere pretender, although Houdini had taken his name in admiration.

prompt: One step would ruin the Gentleman's Peek. Which?
steps: Glimpse the bottom card (the 6♦) while squaring the deck
Ask them to lift off half the deck and look at the top card of their packet
Drop your half squarely on top of their packet
Ask them to shuffle the deck thoroughly
Deal face up until the 6♦ appears, then put the next card aside
explanation: Shuffling would interleave the cards and part the key from their card. Only cuts keep neighbors together.

prompt: Put the Gentleman's Peek in order:
steps: Glimpse the bottom card while tidying the deck
They lift off half the deck and look at its top card
You drop your half on top of their packet
They cut and complete the cut as often as they like
Deal face up; after the key, set the next card aside and reveal it
explanation: The key is learned first, the card is thought of, the key lands on it, the cuts follow and then you find it.

prompt: S. W. Erdnase's identity has been settled beyond doubt.
explanation: The 2001 article says even Dai Vernon never determined the author's true identity, and several rival candidates have been proposed.

prompt: In which city did Erdnase's book first appear in 1902?
options: Chicago
London
Paris
Philadelphia
explanation: It was self-published in Chicago in 1902.

prompt: What did a casino security chief say about card cheats and Erdnase's book?
options: Very few of them have ever read it
Almost all of them learn from it
It was written by one of them
It was banned from casinos
correctAnswer: Very few of them have ever read it
explanation: Ron Conley said that in 35 years around card thieves he found very few had read it; the book influenced magicians more.

prompt: The gap you hold open with your little finger to mark a place in the deck is called a _____.
explanation: A break marks where a packet was replaced so that you can cut to that place.

prompt: Match each person to what the lesson says about them:

pairs.right: The Chicago artist who drew the book's illustrations
Martin Gardner's candidate: a cardsharp who died in 1905
Could quote the book from memory at 88
Published The Sharper Detected and Exposed

explanation: All four appear in the lesson as part of the Erdnase story or the history of card cheating.

prompt: They cut off a packet and look at its bottom card S. You drop it back on the rest with a break under it. What next?
options: Cut at the break so that S becomes the bottom card, then glimpse it
Shuffle the deck and look for S
Ask them to name the card
Turn the deck face up
correctAnswer: Cut at the break so that S becomes the bottom card, then glimpse it
explanation: Lifting everything above the break and putting it under the rest sends S to the bottom, where you can read it.

prompt: One step ruins the thought-of card with a break. Which?
steps: Ask them to cut off a packet and look at its bottom card
Drop the packet on the rest and hold a break under it with your little finger
Lift everything above the break and put it under the rest
Ask them to riffle shuffle the deck several times
Square the deck and glimpse the bottom card
explanation: After the cut at the break the card they saw is at the bottom. A riffle shuffle would lose it.

prompt: Put the thought-of card in order:
steps: They cut off a packet and look at its bottom card
You take the packet back and drop it on the rest, holding a break
You lift the cards above the break and put them under the rest
You glimpse the bottom card
You give clues and name their card
explanation: The card is seen, the break marks it, the cut brings it to the bottom, you glimpse it and then reveal.

prompt: The two accounts of Vernon fooling Houdini say eight times and seven times.
explanation: The Magic profile says eight; the other account says seven. That difference shows how stories drift.

prompt: What is the Ambitious Card?
options: A trick in which a card keeps rising to the top of the deck
A force in which they pick your card
A shuffle that mixes the deck
A trick with a duplicate deck
correctAnswer: A trick in which a card keeps rising to the top of the deck
explanation: The Ambitious Card is a card that keeps coming to the top however often it is lost in the deck.

prompt: In the Ambitious Card, which card does the double lift show?
options: The lower card of the pair: their signed card X
The upper card of the pair: Y
A card chosen by the audience
The bottom card of the deck
correctAnswer: The lower card of the pair: their signed card X
explanation: When the pair is turned as one the lower card ends up face up on top, so they see X.

prompt: At the start of the Ambitious Card, their signed card lies _____ from the top of the deck.
explanation: Y lies over X, so X is second from the top.

prompt: Match each item to its role:

pairs.right: Turns two cards as one
Shows that the card seen twice is the same
He could not be fooled if he saw a trick three times
Chicago banquet, 6 February 1922, in Magic's account

explanation: Each item is part of the routine or of the story told in the lesson.

prompt: A friend says the Vernon and Houdini story is a documented fact. What is the best reply?
options: It is a legend told in versions, and we found no recording or transcript
It was filmed in Chicago
Houdini wrote the number down himself
It was never told by Vernon
correctAnswer: It is a legend told in versions, and we found no recording or transcript
explanation: The sources disagree on the count and neither offers a recording or note by Houdini.

prompt: One step is wrong in the Ambitious Card. Which?
steps: Deal Y aside, have them take the next card X, sign it and return it to the top
Drop Y on top of their card
Double lift to show X face up, signed
Turn the pair face down and push the top card, which is X, into the middle
Snap your fingers and turn over the top card
explanation: After the pair is turned back, the top card is Y. Pushing Y into the middle leaves X on top.

prompt: Put the Ambitious Card first rise in order:
steps: Set Y over their signed card X
Double lift to show X
Turn the pair back face down
Push the top card (Y) into the middle
Snap your fingers and turn over the top card: X
explanation: The set-up puts X second; the double lift shows it; Y is lost in the middle; X is on top for the rise.

prompt: At fourteen, Persi Diaconis left school to tour with Dai Vernon.
explanation: MacTutor says Vernon invited him to join an American tour and he left school without telling his parents.

prompt: At which university was Diaconis appointed assistant professor of statistics after his PhD?
options: Stanford
Oxford
Juilliard
City College of New York
explanation: He was appointed an assistant professor of statistics at Stanford and was a full professor by 1981.

prompt: In Four Suits in Every Four, what must happen after the dealt pile is riffled into the rest?
options: Nothing: no cut and no shuffle
One more riffle
A cut
A thorough overhand shuffle
correctAnswer: Nothing: no cut and no shuffle
explanation: The pattern needs exactly one riffle; a cut or extra shuffle can break it.

prompt: In the four-suit trick, the cards dealt from the top into a pile come out _____ in order.
explanation: Dealing one at a time reverses the pile, so it counts the suit cycle backwards.

prompt: Match each part of the trick to its job:

pairs.right: Counts the suit cycle backwards
Counts the suit cycle forwards
Interleaves the two runs
Cover four consecutive places, so all four suits

explanation: Pile A and the rest run in opposite directions round the cycle, and four consecutive places hold every suit.

prompt: A friend says magic and mathematics are opposites. Which fact from the lesson answers them best?
options: The 1992 shuffling paper lists the analysis of a card trick as a key ingredient
Diaconis never studied mathematics
Magicians cannot count
The Gilbreath principle has no mathematics
correctAnswer: The 1992 shuffling paper lists the analysis of a card trick as a key ingredient
explanation: Bayer and Diaconis name a card trick among the key ingredients of their result on riffle shuffling.

prompt: One step ruins Four Suits in Every Four. Which?
steps: Set the 16 cards in the repeating order club, heart, spade, diamond
Have them deal cards from the top into a pile, one at a time
Have them riffle the pile into the rest, once
Cut the deck so that it looks more mixed
Turn up the top four cards, then the next four
explanation: A cut after the riffle can break the pattern. The principle needs one riffle and nothing else.

prompt: Put the four-suit trick in order:
steps: Set the 16 cards in the repeating suit order and write the slip
They deal some cards from the top into a pile
They riffle the pile into the rest, once
You pick up the deck without cutting
Turn up four cards at a time and open the slip
explanation: The set-up comes first, then the deal reverses the pile, the single riffle follows and the reveal comes last.

prompt: A Si Stebbins stack is learned by memorizing 52 unrelated cards.
explanation: It follows a rule: each card is three higher and the suits repeat in order, so you learn the rule.

prompt: What does a cut do to a cyclic stack?
options: Only changes where the ring is opened, so the order is kept
Destroys the order
Reverses the order
Turns all the cards face up
correctAnswer: Only changes where the ring is opened, so the order is kept
explanation: A cut leaves the ring as it was, which is why you can glimpse one card and know them all.

prompt: In the Si Stebbins stack, which card follows the 4♥?
options: The 7♠
The 5♠
The 7♥
The 4♠
explanation: Add three to the value and move to the next suit: 4♥ is followed by 7♠.

prompt: In the stack each card is _____ higher in value than the one before it.
explanation: Values go up by three, counting round from king to ace.

prompt: Match each name to what the lesson says:

pairs.right: Released his stack in the 1979 pamphlet A Stack to Remember
Released Sinfonia en Mnemonica Mayor in 2000
The order follows a rule
Turns the 52 cards into images in a palace

explanation: Each item is a source or tool for a memorized deck mentioned in the lesson.

prompt: You glimpse the 9♦ at the bottom and they pick the number 7. What is the 7th card from the top?
options: The 4♠
The 4♥
The 5♠
The 7♦
explanation: Add 3 times 7, which is 8 once round the ring, to get 4, and move the suit 7 places, which is 3 places from diamonds: spades.

prompt: One step is wrong in Any Number in a Cut Deck. Which?
steps: Set the deck in stack order beforehand
Let them riffle shuffle the deck
Glimpse the bottom card after the cuts
Ask them to think of a number from 1 to 13
Work out the card and name it
explanation: A riffle shuffle would destroy the stack. Only cuts keep the order.

prompt: A reviewer saw Tamariz perform a Mnemonica routine at a 1990 convention. What does the reviewer say about the audience of magicians?
options: Only a few recognized that the method was in fact a stack
Everyone recognized the stack at once
Nobody enjoyed it
They asked for the order to be printed
correctAnswer: Only a few recognized that the method was in fact a stack
explanation: The review says that despite the sophisticated company only a few recognized that the method was in fact a stack.
